newsitem.title: USA: Columbia shuttle mission extended one day.
newsitem.headline: Columbia shuttle mission extended one day.

text.p: The mission of the space shuttle Columbia will be extended by one day to allow a U.S.-German orbiting observatory to gather more information, NASA officials said on Monday.
The shuttle had been scheduled to return to Earth on Thursday with a landing at its home base in Florida, but shuttle managers decided to extend the mission until Friday, officials said.
"They have made a decision to extend for one day for Orpheus-Spas," said NASA spokeswoman Eileen Hawley.

The Orfeus-Spas telescope, released from the shuttle on Nov. 19, was due to be plucked from orbit by the shuttle crew on Tuesday morning. The space telescope, studying interstellar matter in an effort to learn more about the life cycles of the stars, was trailing Columbia by about 26 miles (42 km).
The telescope retrieval was rescheduled for Wednesday.

Columbia's astronauts have called the Orfeus-Spas programme one of the success stories of a mission marred by the cancellation of two scheduled spacewalks. A jammed hatch kept astronauts Tammy Jernigan and Tom Jones inside the shuttle on Thursday and NASA managers decided on Saturday to cancel their spacewalks.
